options.text: In simplified terms, residence rules determine which ancestral line a child belongs to for inheritance.

Option D assigns the rules to ceremony law, a different domain.
questions.hint: Because norms govern where the couple lives, the concept applies.

questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: examine nuclear family using anthropological evidence

stimulus.body: A household consists of a married couple and their unmarried children, living apart from the parents of either spouse.

questions.stem: Which choice correctly identifies nuclear family in this case?

options.text: In simplified terms, a nuclear family includes three or more generations living in one household.
options.misconception: The couple and their children form a household separate from both sets of parents.

options.text: A partial account holds that a nuclear family is a group of siblings and their spouses with no parents present.
options.misconception: It describes an extended family, which spans generations.

options.text: A nuclear family is a domestic group composed of a couple and their dependent children.
Viewed one way, a nuclear family is a descent group tracing ancestry to a common founder.
options.misconception: It describes a different domestic arrangement, not a couple with children.

questions.explanation: The couple and their children form a household separate from both sets of parents. That is why option C is correct: A nuclear family is a domestic group composed of a couple and their dependent children. The other options fail: Option B describes an extended family, which spans generations. Option D describes a different domestic arrangement, not a couple with children.
questions.hint: Nuclear families are common in industrial societies but are not universal.
